title: Monoidal and scalar comparisons, and abelianity on the representation side.
statement:
/-- Monoidal and scalar comparisons, and abelianity on the representation side.
Source: blueprint `cor-galois-lisse-representations`, proof steps 9-10;
Weil II (1.1.1), (1.1.6); lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9.

Exact Lean statement:
theorem galois_lisse_adic_compatibility
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [∀ P, MulAction G ((FiniteEtale.fiber y).obj P)]
    (c : GaloisLisseFiniteCorrespondence y G)
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] [IsNoetherian Y] [Y.IsSeparated]
    [∀ x : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField x)]
    (Q : Type (u + 1)) [Field Q] [Algebra ℚ_[l] Q] [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] Q]
    (d : GaloisLisseAdicData y G c l Q)
    (hI : galoisIntegralEvaluationAction y G c l Q d)
    (hR : galoisRationalEvaluationAction y G c l Q d)
    (hA : galoisAlgebraicModelScalarExtension y G c l Q d) :
    galoisRationalRepresentationsAbelian y G c l Q d ∧
      galoisAlgebraicRepresentationsAbelian y G c l Q d ∧
      galoisIntegralMonoidal y G c l Q d ∧
      galoisRationalMonoidal y G c l Q d ∧
      galoisAlgebraicMonoidal y G c l Q d ∧
      galoisIntegralScalarExtension y G c l Q d ∧
      galoisRationalScalarExtension y G c l Q d

proof.text:
*(2): scalar extension and the $\Qlb$-level equivalence.* Let $E\subset L$ in $\Qlb$, $e$ the ramification index. For a lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf $\mathcal F$ with fibre $M$, the levels of $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$ are $\mathcal F_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{L,m}$ [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] (3), whose fibres are $M_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{L,m}$ with action $1\otimes\sigma$ by step 5; by [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules] (3) (for $m=en$, $A_{L,en}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_L$) and (1) the limit is $M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, so the fibre functor commutes with scalar extension, naturally and compatibly with $E\subset L\subset L'$. Then for lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves $(E,\mathcal F),(E',\mathcal F')$ with fibres $V_E,V'_{E'}$, steps 8 and this compatibility give $\operatorname{Hom}((E,\mathcal F),(E',\mathcal F'))=\varinjlim_L\operatorname{Hom}_{\pi_1}(V_E\otimes_EL,V'_{E'}\otimes_{E'}L)$. The right side is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\pi_1}(V_E\otimes_E\Qlb,V'_{E'}\otimes_{E'}\Qlb)$: for a fixed $L$ the space $H_L=\operatorname{Hom}_L(V_E\otimes L,V'_{E'}\otimes L)$ is finite-dimensional, its $\pi_1$-invariants are the kernel of the linear map $H_L\to\prod_{g\in S}H_L$, $h\mapsto(gh-h)_g$, for a finite set $S\subset\pi_1$ (finite dimension), and kernels of linear maps commute with the field extension $\otimes_L\Qlb$; hence $\operatorname{Hom}_{\pi_1}(V\otimes\Qlb,V'\otimes\Qlb)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\pi_1}(V\otimes L,V'\otimes L)\otimes_L\Qlb=\varinjlim_{L'}\operatorname{Hom}_{\pi_1}(V\otimes L',V'\otimes L')$. So the functor $(E,\mathcal F)\mapsto\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_E\Qlb$ is fully faithful; its values are $\ell$-adic representations in the sense of [def-pod-l-adic-representations] (3) with $E$-structure $V_E$, and every $\ell$-adic representation has by definition an $E$-structure $V_E$ which is a continuous $E$-representation, hence by step 8 the fibre of some lisse $E$-sheaf, so the functor is essentially surjective. Formalization subproblem: continuous finite-dimensional representations are closed under kernels,
cokernels and finite sums. Restricted actions are continuous for subspaces;
quotient actions descend along the open linear quotient map. For algebraic
coefficients, descend objects and a morphism to a common finite extension
using the finitely many matrix coefficients, and form kernel and cokernel there.
The full-subcategory criterion gives the two abelian structures.
For integral tensors, the finite-level fibre tensor maps are equivariant by
c.finiteTensor and the integral evaluation formula. The finite-module tensor
reduction and reconstruction theorems identify their limit with the tensor of
integral fibres. The same construction for units and scalar extension gives
canonical comparisons. Their constraint diagrams can be checked after every
finite-level projection, hence hold by separatedness. Rationalize them; the
rational evaluation formula gives equivariance on pure tensors. Extend to
algebraic coefficients over a common finite field, using the model scalar
comparison. Naturality and constraint diagrams hold on the generators and pass
through localization. This supplies the specified monoidal structures and the
natural integral/rational scalar comparisons, without postulating tensor clauses.

proof.text:
*(2): exactness, tensor products and the unit.* Continuous $E$-representations form an abelian category: the kernel and image of an equivariant linear map are stable subspaces with continuous (restricted) action, and the cokernel $V/W$ has continuous action because $\pi_1\times V\to\pi_1\times V/W$ is an open surjection (a projection of a product times the open linear surjection $V\to V/W$) through which the continuous map $\pi_1\times V\to V/W$ factors; likewise $\ell$-adic representations (a map between representations defined over $E$ and $E'$ is defined over some $L\supset E,E'$ by step 9, and kernel and cokernel are then defined over $L$). An additive category equivalent to an abelian category is abelian, and an equivalence of abelian categories preserves kernels and cokernels, so the equivalences at the levels $E$ and $\Qlb$ (additive by steps 8 and 9) are exact. Tensor products: the fibres of $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G=(\mathcal F_n\otimes\mathcal G_n)_n$ are $M_n\otimes_{A_{E,n}}N_n$ with the diagonal action by step 4, so by [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules] (1) and (3) its fibre is $\varprojlim_n(M\otimes N)/\varpi_E^n=M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}N$ with the diagonal action; the unit $(\underline{A_{E,n}})_n$ has fibre $\varprojlim A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E$ with trivial action by step 4. Tensoring with $E$ and passing to the colimit over $L$ (formed with the scalar extension of step 9) gives the same at the levels $E$ and $\Qlb$, where the diagonal action on $V\otimes W$ is continuous because it is so on $M\otimes N$, an open lattice. Formalization subproblem: continuous finite-dimensional representations are closed under kernels,
cokernels and finite sums. Restricted actions are continuous for subspaces;
quotient actions descend along the open linear quotient map. For algebraic
coefficients, descend objects and a morphism to a common finite extension
using the finitely many matrix coefficients, and form kernel and cokernel there.
The full-subcategory criterion gives the two abelian structures.
For integral tensors, the finite-level fibre tensor maps are equivariant by
c.finiteTensor and the integral evaluation formula. The finite-module tensor
reduction and reconstruction theorems identify their limit with the tensor of
integral fibres. The same construction for units and scalar extension gives
canonical comparisons. Their constraint diagrams can be checked after every
finite-level projection, hence hold by separatedness. Rationalize them; the
rational evaluation formula gives equivariance on pure tensors. Extend to
algebraic coefficients over a common finite field, using the model scalar
comparison. Naturality and constraint diagrams hold on the generators and pass
through localization. This supplies the specified monoidal structures and the
natural integral/rational scalar comparisons, without postulating tensor clauses.

mathlib_searches.query: An equivalence between finite locally constant module sheaves and finite continuous representations, compatible with stalks and tensor products
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, primarily Mathlib.Condensed.Discrete.Module; no scheme-etale or adic correspondence. Earlier fundamental-group query found the abstract functorToContAction equivalence only.

mathlib_searches.query: Integral adic sheaves and continuous finite dimensional p-adic representations, tensor products and scalar extension
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits on AdicCompletion, including ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian, but no sheaf-representation equivalence or monoidal comparison.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Useful finite-module infrastructure already covered by the declared adic-limit dependency; no exact match.

mathlib_searches.results: LocalSystems proves the finite commutative-ring equivalence; it does not cover all noncommutative finite rings nor the adic clauses. EquivalenceInternalModule proves transport of internal modules, and its finite-action identification is stated. No adic-category equivalence was found.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Reuse the declared modules for the parts they cover; the missing comparison/glue is stated here.
